results.title: TQCompressor: Improving Tensor Decomposition Methods in Neural Networks Via Permutations
results.venue: Conference on Multimedia Information Processing and Retrieval
results.abstract: We introduce TQCompressor a neural network model compression method using enhanced tensor decompositions. We propose a permutation-based improvement to Kronecker decomposition, reducing the loss in model expressivity typically associated with compression. Applied to $\mathbf{GPT-2}_{small}$, this results in the TQCompressedGPT-2 model with 81 million parameters, down from 124 million. Enhanced through multi-step knowledge distillation on 3.1% of OpenWebText, TQCompressedGPT-2 outperforms DistilGPT-2 and KnGPT-2. We made TQCompressedGPT-2 publicly available.

results.title: A 198.7 μJ/token Block Diffusion LLM Processor with Mask Token Similarity-Based Activation Reuse
results.venue: International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
results.abstract: This paper presents an energy-efficient diffusion-based large language model processor. Diffusion-based large language models have attained significant attention for their computational parallelism, which enables both high token generation speed and energy efficiency. However, their inherent block-based architecture still contains redundancies that can be further optimized. The proposed processor achieves high energy efficiency and low token generation latency with three key features as solutions: 1) Mask token similarity-based activation reuse (MTAR) to reduce computation energy of global prefill stage by 70.6%, 2) Continuous confidence-based mixed precision (CCMP) to allow 94.2% of the local block decoding stage workload to be processed with low-precision activation. 3) Reordering shared bit-slice core (RSBC) architecture to reduce computation energy of local block decoding stage by 46.3%. The proposed processor is implemented in 28 nm CMOS technology and achieves 32.8 TOPS peak throughput with 10.1 TOPS/W. In sum, 198.7 μJ/token highly energy-efficient diffusion-based LLM processor can be achieved on the GSM8K dataset.
